newsitem.title: USA: Dole says action against Saddam should be decisive.
newsitem.headline: Dole says action against Saddam should be decisive.

text.p: Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole said on Tuesday he hoped President Bill Clinton's missile strike against Iraq marked the start of decisive action to curtail Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein's power.

"I trust that this development marks the beginning of decisive action by the United States to curtail the power of Saddam Hussein, and the end of his defiance of the international community and of his atrocities against the Kurdish minority in Iraq," he said in a statement.
"The actions taken will be read by dictators and would-be aggressors around the globe," Dole added. "Hence we must be resolute."

Dole, who has blamed the latest flareup on a failure of Clinton's leadership in dealing with Saddam, said he stood "four-square behind" U.S. men and women involved in the U.S. military action against Iraq.

Dole said the goal of the U.S. action should be the withdrawal of Saddam's troops from the Kurdish-populated north of Iraq, the release of Kurdish prisoners, and a halt to interference by both Iraq and Iran among the Kurds.

In addition, the action should be aimed at reestablishing U.N. weapons inspection efforts "and an end to Saddam's support of international terrorism," he said in the statement released from Salt Lake City, Utah, where Dole is on the campaign trail.
Dole, in remarks over the weekend, had accused Clinton of unwisely accepting the planned relaxation of sanctions on Iraqi oil sales.
He also had accused Clinton of doing little recently to protest Saddams's continued obstruction of nuclear weapons inspectors except to "join in weak statements by the U.N. Security Council."
